text:
The Tamsin Reservoir repair cost 48 million, according to a filing released Thursday by Veyra Waterworks. The work, completed in late October, covered reinforced lining, gate replacement and slope stabilization after seepage was detected in March. Veyra said the project came in 6% above its original 45 million budget because of supply delays and emergency dewatering.

Chief engineer Alon Price said the reservoir is back at full capacity and will re-enter routine rotation next week. Analysts at Bracken & Sloane said the bill underscores rising maintenance costs across the water-utilities sector, where aging concrete assets and tighter safety rules are pushing more capex into repairs rather than expansion.
